📖 Game script

Buffalo scores 33.7 points a game at 6.5 yards per play and gets a HIGH secondary grade against a New England defense playing without Christian Gonzalez (out). Josh Allen (243+ passing at −101, and −136 to score, tied with James Cook III for the shortest touchdown price) and Cook (86+ rushing at +101) build the lead, with Dalton Kincaid (52+) working the middle. New England averages 12 points with a −5 turnover margin; Drake Maye leans on Hunter Henry and Romeo Doubs (40+) on the MEDIUM side. Allen's knee caps the margin: EC took his passing under 242.5 and Steve Fezzik calls him banged up. Buffalo by six, inside the 7.

🧠 Why the card leans this way

Read in full, the expert columns lean New England 6–4. NE: Steve Fezzik (Even Money) at +7, Andrew Erickson at +7.5 (New England has covered 5 of the last 6 in the series), and four VSiN best bets: Steve Makinen and Dave Tuley at +6.5, Matt Youmans and Wes Reynolds at +7; Ross Tucker leans NE. BUF: Action Network, BettingPros, Sharp or Square and Mike Florio (Bills 34–21), most at −6.5. Evan Abrams' primer has eight systems firing in this game, five on the New England spread (great-condition divisional road dogs, underdogs off a blowout loss and fading the public after a poor offensive game among them) and two on the under; as a 3-point-plus underdog, Mike Vrabel is 30–18–2 against the spread. Splits are public on Buffalo, 60% of tickets and 65% of money, no sharp gap. The Action Network open was −6.5; the line now sits on the key number 7. On that evidence the projection moves a point toward New England each way (Buffalo by six, down from eight), so the lean flips from Buffalo-without-the-7 to NE +7, with Cook to score as the Buffalo-side prop. The projected 48 is under the 50 total and both under systems agree, a small under lean; BettingPros' over 48.5 is now a point and a half worse. Card: NE +7 is a leg of the Slot 5 Hybrid. NE +6.5 is a SuperContest alternate.

⚠️ What breaks it

Allen's knee limits his running and Buffalo wins by a field goal. Ray Davis is questionable, which thins the backfield behind Cook. Maye gets enough protection to find Henry late for a backdoor cover. Wind gusts reach 20 mph, not enough to change the script.
